narrative.overview: A technical switchboard printed by an editorial studio. Near-black paper holds warm ivory information; restrained gold identifies active paths, contracts, and decisive words. Diagrams are the explanatory surface, and ledger rules keep protocol material scannable.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial scale paired with precise protocol labels.
Gold reserved for signals, active state, and architectural invariants.
Hairline structure instead of container-heavy cards.
Native HTML, CSS, and SVG diagrams with accessible text equivalents.
One moving signal path, disabled for reduced-motion preferences.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Gold identifies meaning or movement; it never fills generic decoration.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Display type argues; body and protocol type prove.

rules.name: The Flat Signal Rule
rules.body: A state change alters line, fill, or text role—not elevation.

dos: Do give each slide one architectural claim and one proving diagram.
Do reserve monospace for actual protocol, schema, timing, and state data.
Do preserve content order across desktop and mobile.
Do keep dense diagrams horizontally scrollable when collapsing would destroy meaning.
Do use gold to expose direction, authority, or an invariant.
donts: Don't replace diagrams with decorative cards or generic icon grids.
Don't use glow, gradient text, or shadows to imply technical importance.
Don't shrink labels below readable sizes to force a desktop matrix onto mobile.
Don't let motion become the only way to understand dataflow.
Don't introduce additional accent hues without a new semantic state.
